Job Summary

Designs, develops and manages the lifecycle of a product or group of products from concept to launch to end of life. Translates market opportunities and customer demand into viable products and services that differentiate Equinix in the market. Sets the vision and strategy for their product ensuring it is competitively positioned and customer-centric. Manages the product roadmap including features, upgrades and maintenance of the product or product line. Works cross functionally with user experience, engineering, operations, solution architects, marketing and others to design, build and launch new products and/or product features.

Responsibilities

Own model selection

• Define how Equinix chooses models for each application. Criteria include task quality on our own evals, cost per task, latency, context length, tool-use ability, hardware footprint, license terms and data-handling requirements
• Maintain a recommended-model catalogue across open-weight and proprietary models, with clear guidance on when each fits
• Track new model releases, benchmark them against Equinix workloads, and decide when an upgrade is worth the switching cost

Lead model customization

• Set the playbook for adapting models, from prompt and context engineering and retrieval to supervised fine-tuning, parameter-efficient methods (such as LoRA), preference optimization, reinforcement learning from feedback, distillation and quantization
• Help teams choose the lightest technique that meets the bar. Prompting and retrieval come first, and training is used where it clearly pays off
• Define the data strategy behind tuning, including curation, labeling, synthetic data generation, deduplication, and protecting against leakage between training and evaluation data

Build the platform

• Own the roadmap for a shared model customization platform covering data preparation, training, evaluation, registry, deployment and lifecycle management
• Partner with infrastructure and engineering teams on GPU capacity, training and serving stacks, inference optimization, and cost controls
• Make tuned models reproducible and supportable, with versioned data, configs and checkpoints, clear ownership, and rollback

Partner with vertical teams to launch

• Work with business and domain teams to scope use cases, pick models, design tuning experiments and launch to production
• Turn early wins into repeatable patterns, templates and services that the next team can reuse
• Run model launch reviews covering quality, safety, cost, performance and operational readiness

Measure and improve

• Define the evaluations every model must pass before launch: task-specific quality, regression against the base model, safety, robustness and cost and latency targets
• Partner with the Agent Intelligence team so tuned models are measured in production and feedback flows back into better data and better models
• Report the impact of customization in terms leaders care about, such as quality gained, cost saved, latency reduced and risk avoided

Govern models responsibly

• Set standards for license review, model provenance, data rights, model documentation, red-teaming and approval to deploy
• Make sure confidential and customer data used in tuning is handled within Equinix’s security, privacy and regulatory requirements

Lead across the organization

• Be Equinix’s go-to product leader on model selection and customization, and influence teams you don’t manage
• Write the strategy, specs and executive briefs that align engineering, data science, infrastructure, security and business leaders

In your first year, you will

• Publish Equinix’s model selection framework and recommended-model catalogue, backed by benchmarks on our own workloads
• Launch a shared customization platform that takes a team from data to a deployed, evaluated, tuned model
• Ship tuned open-weight models into production with at least two vertical teams, with measured gains over the baseline
• Establish a governance process for licensing, data rights and approval to deploy that teams can move through quickly

Qualifications

• 7+ years across product management, engineering or applied ML, including 3+ years as a product manager on AI/ML, data or infrastructure platforms
• Hands-on experience customizing and shipping open-weight models in production, such as fine-tuning, parameter-efficient tuning, preference optimization, distillation or quantization
• Deep practical knowledge of prompt and context engineering and retrieval-augmented generation, and sound judgment about when to use them instead of training
• Experience selecting models for real applications, weighing quality, cost, latency, hardware and licensing
• Strong evaluation skills, including building task-specific evals, avoiding train/test leakage, and telling a real improvement from noise
• Working knowledge of the model training and serving stack (for example PyTorch, Hugging Face, and inference servers such as vLLM or SGLang) and of GPU cost and capacity trade-offs
• Comfort reading and writing Python, running experiments, and reviewing training and evaluation results yourself
• Ability to lead without authority across engineering, science, infrastructure and business teams, and to explain trade-offs clearly to senior leaders

Nice to have

• Experience with reinforcement learning from human or AI feedback, or with reward modeling
• Experience with synthetic data generation and data curation at scale
• Experience with tool-use or agentic fine-tuning, or with function-calling models
• Experience with open-weight model licensing, model governance or responsible AI programs
• Experience running models in private, hybrid or on-premises environments, or with data residency requirements
• Experience in regulated industries such as financial services
• A degree in computer science, engineering, machine learning or another quantitative field, or equivalent experience. Publications or open-source contributions are a plus

What this role is not

This is not a research scientist role, and it’s not a pure prompt-engineering role. You will own the product: the framework, the platform and the launches. You will be accountable for tuned models that are measurably better, cheaper or faster in production.

What success looks like

• Every team knows which model to start with and why, and model choices are backed by Equinix’s own benchmarks
• Teams reach for fine-tuning only when it pays off, and when they do, the platform makes it fast and repeatable
• Tuned models in production beat their baselines on quality, cost or latency, and the gains are measured and reported
• Model launches pass a clear, quick governance process with no surprises on licensing, data rights or safety
• Equinix builds lasting expertise in running and improving its own models

Why this role matters

Choosing and adapting models well is becoming a core capability for any company building with AI. Open-weight models let Equinix put the right model on each problem, control cost and data, and build behavior that general-purpose models can’t match. You will make that capability real, repeatable and trusted across the company.

At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Lyft connects people to transportation to change the way we live and get around our communities. We are looking for product managers who bring exceptional creative, strategic, and analytical skills to drive forward a best in class product. Product management at Lyft leads the integration of engineering, data science, and design to achieve the company's vision for reinventing transportation. We are looking for entrepreneurial and passionate Product Managers to innovate and execute across a rapidly growing, fast paced company and industry.

Pricing is the primary economic engine of Lyft's marketplace — a high-precision, real-time system that processes millions of fare calculations per hour, balancing rider affordability, driver earnings, and Lyft's sustainable growth. The Pricing team sits at the intersection of the marketplace, mediating between rider demand and driver supply, and is a core pillar of the Rider Organization.

The Base Pricing Team owns the systems that set the base price of a Lyft ride for every ride type, region, and ride intent. Behind these base prices is a machine-learning and optimization stack that predicts how the Lyft marketplace responds to price, translates the cost of serving a ride into a price, and recommends price changes across hundreds of markets every week. Base prices are the foundation of every fare, and they set the reference point that dynamic pricing and rider discounts build on.

The team serves two sets of customers: riders, who should see prices that are fair, competitive, and matched to what they value; and the analysts and market managers who use our models and tools to set pricing strategy.

Responsibilities:

As the Staff Product Manager for Base Pricing, you will own the vision and roadmap for how Lyft sets base prices, and define the success metrics that measure it. That includes:

• Determining the optimal granularity at which Lyft sets base prices (e.g., by time, location, and type of trip)

• Improving how our base price optimization engine works with downstream dynamic pricing systems to better respond to real-time market conditions

• Re-evaluating how costs to fulfill a ride impact prices

• Jointly optimizing prices across ride types, so that standard, alternative modes, and scheduled rides are priced as one portfolio

• Making our impact estimation models accurate and trusted by market management teams

• Evolving base pricing to function in a hybrid network with autonomous vehicles

• Work closely with cross-functional stakeholders (engineers, scientists, analysts), and partner teams (Driver Earnings, Verticals, Market Management) to align on a shared vision, define requirements, and prioritize inbound requests.

• Communicate roadmaps, experiment results, and pricing decisions clearly to audiences from partner teams up to Lyft's executive team.

Experience:

• 8+ years of product management or relevant experience, with significant time spent on algorithmic, data-driven, pricing, or marketplace products
